reasons: v0 has the best raw coverage (123 tokens with 2+ usable items vs 115 and 114), but part of it comes from items inside the concept: where Carthage was founded and where it lies (also through thage/Qart-hadasht), the Etruscans and Tuscany, the Gaulish language, Cleopatra's dynasty and capital, and Dante's Virgil. It also has giveaways (four o'clock flower -> late afternoon, Times New Roman -> The Times, Thessalonica -> Thessalonians, consuls -> Consulates, Marcus Welby M.D.) and quote-forced items ("molluscs", "tusks", "(mausoleum)"). v1 removes those by cutting Carthage, Cleopatra, Etruscan, llus and tus down to the clean outside uses. It still has smaller leaks (Belisarius vs the Vandals in North Africa, the Tunis-Carthage airport, the Ptolemies of Hellenistic Egypt, an Actium distractor). It also repeats subjects across tokens (Hagia Sophia, Istanbul as the answer, Napoleon as First Consul twice, Caesar the chimp) and uses citation tails like "(Anton Chekhov, 1900)". v2 fixes all of these. It reclassifies rinus and thage as exclusive, which I think is right: the only outside uses are an obscure binomial and an airport named after the ancient site. It replaces trivia (Isandlwana, Honorary Consul, Foreign Legion HQ, Sandman) with school-level facts and moves the no-space tokens to the more natural appositive style. I checked the facts of every v2 item and found none wrong. Each has exactly one correct option, and base_acc is the highest of the three (0.925). v2 costs almost nothing in coverage compared with v1 (114 vs 115 tokens with 2+ usable items, 59 vs 60 with 4), and most of v0's extra coverage is items that break neutrality. So v2 is the best version on the top three rubric criteria. Its remaining weakness, shared by all versions, is items where a removable modifier token (Mesopotamian, Hellenistic, a bracketed Constantinople) adds nothing because the rest of the question already gives the answer. I list the clearest of these below.
residual_problems: Which Italian poet, author of the Divine Comedy, is buried in Ravenna?: token not essential: 'author of the Divine Comedy' gives Dante without Ravenna
The Basilica of San Vitale in Ravenna depicts which Byzantine emperor: token not essential: the emperor married to Theodora is Justinian regardless of Ravenna
Byzantium stood on which strait linking the Black Sea: token not essential: the strait linking the Black Sea and the Sea of Marmara is the Bosporus by definition
Cleopatra's Needle in London stands beside which river?: token not essential: any central London landmark stands beside the Thames
Pompey, the naval city on England's south coast, is home: token not essential: Nelson's preserved flagship is HMS Victory whatever the city
Mark Twain grew up in Hannibal, a town on: token not essential: Mark Twain alone points to the Mississippi
Which Icelandic singer starred in Lars von Trier's Dancer: token not essential: Bjork is the only Icelandic solo singer among the options

The Hellenistic statue Venus de Milo is displayed in which: token not essential: Venus de Milo alone gives the Louvre

According to the verse (Romans 6:23), the wages of sin: token not essential: the quoted verse itself gives eternal life
